questions.stem: True or false: The cranial dura is anatomically different from the spinal dura.
questions.why: The cranial dura has two layers (endosteal and meningeal) with venous sinuses between; the spinal dura has one, with an epidural space.

questions.stem: True or false: The opercula include the gyrus rectus.
questions.why: The opercula (frontal, parietal, temporal) cover the insula; the gyrus rectus is on the orbital surface.

questions.why: It forms part of the floor of the body.

questions.stem: True or false: The interventricular foramen (of Monro) is closely related to the crus of the fornix.
questions.why: Its anterior boundary is the COLUMN of the fornix.

questions.why: Splenium lesions cause alexia without agraphia; alien hand follows anterior callosal or frontal lesions.

questions.why: It compresses the anterior cerebral artery.

questions.stem: True or false: In transcalvarial herniation, brain tissue is squeezed through the foramen magnum.
questions.why: It herniates through a defect in the skull (e.g. a fracture or craniectomy). Through the foramen magnum is tonsillar herniation.

questions.stem: True or false: The corpora quadrigemina are seen on the ventral surface of the midbrain.
questions.why: They are on the DORSAL surface (tectum).

questions.why: Brainstem lesions give IPSILATERAL cranial nerve palsy with contralateral hemiplegia.

questions.why: It is area 4. Area 6 is premotor; area 8 is the frontal eye field.

questions.why: Inferior frontal gyrus (areas 44, 45). Wernicke's is on the superior temporal gyrus.

questions.why: Parietal (somatosensory association) lobe.

questions.why: True.
